title: Attune
pitch: Design physical products with your browser agent, find who can make it
about_excerpt: Design physical products with your browser agent, find who can make it Like Comment Story Updates Attune Design Attune Let the design find its maker. Inspiration I came into this challenge from a UX/UI and product design background. At first I kept asking: what can an agent do on a website? While building Attune, a better question took over: What should the person and the agent do together? A person may be better at looking at a design, moving something by eye, and deciding what feels right. An agent can help with exact values, repeated edits, relationships, checks, and multi-step work. The useful part is when both work on the same object , without the person having to explain that object again and again. That became Attune. What Attune does Attune is a shared workspace for designing physical products . The person gets the visual canvas. The browser agent gets WebMCP tools. Both work on the same underlying design. If I already selected something, I should not need to describe which part I mean. If the design already knows a measurement, the agent should not guess it from the screen. If I change something myself, the agent should continue from the new state. The goal is not “AI, finish the whole design for me.” It is closer to: I decide → the agent helps → I adjust → Attune checks → we continue. Why WebMCP here? A 2D engineering sketch is more than pixels. It contains entities, dimensions, constraints, groups, solver state, versions, and relationships between parts. A small edit can also affect what happens later. Without a structured interface, an agent has to reconstruct too much of that from the visible UI. With WebMCP, Attune can give the agent direct actions over the same design state the person is using. That lets the agent answer four useful questions: What am I working on? What can I change here? What would this change affect? What can happen next? Attune also does not expose one giant toolbox on every page. Design tools appear while editing. Manufacturing tools appear later. Buyer and Maker actions stay separate. Important commercial actions still require human confirmation. Chrome WebMCP WebMCP tools Not every tool is active at once. The current page, project state, and the person's access decide what is exposed. Surface Tool What it does / why it is exposed Dashboard inspect_projects Reads accessible projects and their current stage. Dashboard create_project Creates a blank or template project when allowed. Dashboard open_project Opens an accessible project on the right surface. Dashboard inspect_notifications Reads recent activity so the agent can find what needs attention. Dashboard open_notification Opens one notification and navigates to its authorized project surface. Design inspect_context Reads the current selection, IDs, versions, nearby geometry, constraints, solver state, and unseen human changes. Design forecast_change Previews what one proposed design action would do before anything is committed. Design modify_geometry Creates or changes real sketch geometry, including parametric recipes, radius edits, transforms, node moves, trims, deletes, and groups. Design constrain_geometry Adds or removes dimensions and engineering relationships such as tangency. Design check_design Checks solver and validation state after an edit. Manufacturing find_makers Compares the current design with Maker capability so the design itself can be used to ask who can make it. Workspace navigate_workspace Moves between valid Attune surfaces without using navigation to grant new authority. Manufacturing manage_manufacturing_request Configures, submits, quotes, requests changes, and accepts work when the operation is valid for the current role and state. Commerce inspect_commerce_pipeline Reads the request → quote → acceptance → Shopify Draft Order chain without customer contact details. Commerce prepare_customer_checkout Retrieves a verified checkout handoff only after confirmation and only when checkout is available. Workspace manage_account Exposes account/setup operations that make sense from the current workspace state. Settings inspect_account_setup Checks Buyer setup and connected Maker stores without returning private contact data. Settings start_shopify_connection Starts Shopify OAuth while the merchant still approves permissions themselves. Settings select_shopify_location Selects a real active Shopify location for the connected Maker. Settings inspect_shopify_orders Reads recent Draft Orders and their Attune version bindings without customer PII or checkout URLs. Settings open_shopify_admin Opens a previously inspected Draft Order in the Maker's Shopify Admin. Settings open_maker_workspace Opens Maker profile, incoming requests, or accepted jobs. Judge review inspect_review_flow Explains the seeded review path and why later stages are locked or available. Judge review open_review_control_center Opens the judge control center without changing workflow state. Judge review reset_judge_workspace Resets only the seeded judge workspace after explicit confirmation. The important part is not the number of tools. The tools follow the work. Co-creation, not autopilot Building the design side taught me that precise design is not really a one-prompt problem. Even a simple request can depend on what should stay fixed when something else moves. Recent Autodesk research on AI CAD editing points to the same problem: current models are improving, but matching the designer's exact intent is still difficult. That helped clarify the roles: The person provides intent and judgement. The agent helps interpret and carry out the request. The application owns the exact result. Attune works with real 2D geometry and constraints rather than treating the canvas as only a picture. Autodesk Research - AI CAD editing Why manufacturing? Manufacturing made this interaction more meaningful because a design action can have consequences outside the screen. Moving one feature can affect a constraint. It can affect whether a Maker can make the part. A later design edit can also make an older quote belong to the wrong version. So I started thinking about WebMCP actions as steps on a path: see the work → understand the change → check the result → know what can happen next The model can help understand what I want. It should not invent whether something is actually manufacturable. The design becomes the query Once the design is ready, another problem appears: Who can make this? Today that often becomes another translation step: “CNC shop”, “aluminium fabrication”, “laser cutting”. But the design already contains more useful information than those words: geometry, dimensions, material, quantity, and requirements. The longer-term idea behind Attune is: Let the design itself become the query. The person can then add what matters: prefer somebody nearby, need it quickly, preserve these mounting points, or show a specialist if nobody local fits. And Makers are not always sellers. live_observation.first_impression: A Chrome for Developers documentation page about Web MCP and agents, with explanatory sections and links to demos; it is not the Attune product workspace.
live_observation.action_attempted: Clicked the listed WebMCP demo link in the documentation.
live_observation.after_state: The page remained documentation content after navigation/click handling; no Attune design canvas was exposed.
live_observation.notes: Demo URL resolves to the general Chrome WebMCP documentation rather than the claimed Attune app.
